title: Verify the spend ceiling stops computer work on live development
description:
**Phase 5.** Not a demo. The same class of check as refuse-not-fallback.

---

## Why this card exists

`chatticus-43e64c` and `chatticus-6a9e97` are closed, and both closed on **green CI, not live verification**. From `6a9e97`'s closing note:

> Live development still needs a ThinTurn/web deploy plus an org with a ceiling and rollup rows before a member can see the banner on `dev.chattic.us`. Closing the card on green merge; live seed is a follow-up on the epic **if we want a timed demo**.

Closing on green was reasonable. Framing the live run as an optional demo is the part worth revisiting, because **the ceiling is the safety property**, and this project has already established a standard for those.

## The standard already set

`chatticus-2f2d87` promoted refuse-not-fallback from an in-memory Gherkin scenario to a production result, and the runbook now says so explicitly:

> Refuse-not-fallback (production-verified, 2026-09-07)... Cite this section for any customer-facing claim. It is not only a card comment.

That was the right call, and the reason applies here identically. Both properties protect a customer from a cost they did not agree to. Both are unfalsifiable from the outside until they fire.

## Why green CI is weaker evidence here than usual

Every real defect found this week passed at one layer and broke at a seam:

| Found | Green at | Broken at |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal missing | spec and docs | no tool existed |
| File tools | both layers individually | never connected |
| Customer image | role built for customer ECR | stack pulled from Anthus |
| Host start | `RunTask` returned | task never reached RUNNING |

The ceiling has more seams than most of those: rollup rows, a deploy, an org record, the worker's refusal path, and a banner. Gherkin covers the decision logic; it does not cover whether the rollup that feeds it is actually populated in a deployed environment.

## Why now

The operator throttle is gone. `chatticus-9c8dbf`, `chatticus-070cb4` and `chatticus-7622fd` closed, so a customer can self-provision, and `run_terminal` is grantable on a computer that runs cross-account. The product can start compute on someone else's bill by design. **The brake for that is this ceiling, and it has never been observed stopping anything outside a test suite.**

## What to run

Seed an org on development with a ceiling and rollup rows above it, then attempt computer work.

- New computer work is **refused**, fail-closed.
- The organization stays **enabled** — `6a9e97`'s whole point is that crossing the ceiling stops computer work, not the org.
- The member sees the banner on `dev.chattic.us`.
- Record what a member can actually do next. If the answer is "contact an operator", that is a person-step and belongs in the invitation-rate math alongside `chatticus-c54569`.

## Related, and worth confirming in the same pass

`#337`'s review noted the owner-raise Gherkin hits the kernel rather than the PATCH route. If an owner cannot raise their own ceiling through the product, hitting the ceiling converts an unbounded bill into a support ticket — a different bottleneck, not a solved problem.

## Done when

The runbook has a ceiling section citable for customer-facing claims, in the same form as refuse-not-fallback: what was attempted, what was refused, what stayed enabled, and what the member could do next.
